title: Field network wiring notelet - vpc/onprem night shift
document:
2025-02-16 23:40 - Night shift quick brain dump

Context: Third day at AcmeCorp rack install (site B). Customer has hybrid: VPC peering to our private control plane + onprem appliance behind customer firewall. Notes below are for handover and for me to pick up tomorrow.

Summary observations (top of mind)
- Wire pairs: two redundant uplinks from top-of-rack (ToR-3) to customer leaf switch (Arista-7060). LACP configured but we saw intermittent flapping on port 1/23. Suspect SFP mismatch (10G SR vs 10G LR).
- Management VLAN: 192.168.240.0/24 (static IPs for appliances). Customer uses .2-.10 for their infra; we are assigned .50-.58. Documented in ticket but double-check with networking team before final IP commit.
- KMS endpoint must be allowed outbound to kms.acme.local:443 from appliance management interface (customer NAT). Packet capture shows TLS handshake drops at their perimeter firewall (stateful timeout).
- Proxy: customer uses forward proxy (squid) for external egress; installer didn't pick up proxy env automatically. Need to add proxy env to /etc/redwood/installer.conf when doing next retry.
- Kernel/driver: hosts are on Ubuntu 22.04 w/ nvidia-driver 535.11. Tried install and the driver package failed on one host (kernel header mismatch). Host kernel: 5.15.0-1016-generic. Installer expects headers for 5.15.0-1020. Workaround: apt-get update && apt-get dist-upgrade scheduled; coordinate with Acme ops (they requested no reboot until after maintenance window).

Commands and snippets I used (copy-paste friendly)
- Check link and SFP type: ethtool -i eth0 && ethtool -S eth0 ; ethtool -P eth1
- Show LACP state on Arista: show lacp counters && show interfaces Ethernet1/23 transceiver
- Quick tcpdump for TLS handshake drops: TCPDUMP: sudo tcpdump -i bond0 host kms.acme.local and port 443 -w /tmp/kms-handshake.pcap
- Add proxy env for installer: sudo tee /etc/redwood/installer.env <<'EOF'
http_proxy=http://proxy.acme.local:3128
https_proxy=http://proxy.acme.local:3128
no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost,192.168.240.0/24
EOF

Unresolved blockers (need action)
1) SFP mismatch / LACP flapping on port 1/23 - contact Acme network and request swap/test with compatible SR module or force 10G full on trunk. (Assigned: Liam)
2) KMS TLS failure - firewall stateful timeout or MTU problem? Need perimeter team to run packet capture at firewall egress. (Assigned: Priya)
3) Kernel headers mismatch on node-03 - can't install nvidia driver without reboot. Customer forbids reboot until Monday window. We need a temporary CPU-only service until reboot. (Assigned: Maya)

Site-specific reminders for next handoff
- Rack ID B-12 (row 4), PDU A feeds racks 42 & 43. Customer power budget: 7kW per rack — don't add more GPUs than listed.
- Serial console access: use com port via BMC IP (192.168.240.56). Default creds changed to acme!R@nd0m, recorded in vault (ask SRE to fetch rotation secret).
- Staging mirror: onsite mirror for apt at http://apt-mirror.acme.local; add to apt sources to avoid slow external downloads during installs.
- Air gap plan: if customer triggers, we have offline installer tar at /media/usb/onprem_v2.tar.gz (verified checksum: sha256: 9f7a3b...). Bring the thumb drive to site if asked.

Quick handover checklist for morning tech (short)
- [ ] Confirm LACP transceiver types and swap SFP if necessary (ask net ops to log MACs swapped).
- [ ] Re-run installer with proxy env after apt mirror added.
- [ ] Capture firewall egress pcap for TLS failure (kms.acme.local:443).
- [ ] Coordinate with customer on maintenance window for kernel reboot (node-03).
- [ ] Update Confluence note with final IP mapping and PDU load numbers.

Notes to self / reminders
- Remember to push kernel headers change to our installer repo to auto-detect and warn if headers mismatch (GH PR idea).
- Make a small helper script to validate SFP compatibility (based on transceiver vendor string) and warn during preflight.
- Ask security to verify HSM connectivity test passes after KMS open on 443 (not just reachability — need TLS client cert handshake test).

Random troubleshooting timeline (ordered)
- 18:10 — Arrived, verified rack labels and power feeds. Confirmed PDU meters match expected load.
- 19:05 — Attempted installer run v2.4.1, failed on docker pull (timeout) — switched apt to local mirror, retried.
- 20:22 — Nvidia driver failed on node-03 (header mismatch). Put node-03 into maintenance mode in console to keep scheduler from sending jobs.
- 21:15 — Observed LACP flaps; swapped physical cable with spare, no change. Noted SFP vendor mismatch. Logged to JIRA-CUST-2384.
- 22:50 — Attempted proxy config; installer progressed further but failed at KMS handshake. Saved pcap for Priya.

When you pick this up:
- Read the pcap (pcap file on site /tmp/kms-handshake.pcap) — filter for TLS alerts and capture the initial ClientHello. If the ClientHello is missing, we likely have NAT or proxy stripping.
- Ask Acme network to run show run | include interface Ethernet1/23 and check transceiver vendor string on both ends.

Reference links I keep returning to:
- Confluence: Onprem Handoff Checklist (link above)
- Installer repo: github.com/redwood-inference/onprem-installer PR#72 notes
- JIRA-CUST-2384: ticket with SFP logs, pcap attached

End note: keep this doc small and noisy — it's a working memory, not the canonical runbook. Move final steps to Confluence once stable.

-- Maya
